newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures seen trying for record high in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures seen trying for record high in Tokyo.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures are expected to move in a tight range on Wednesday as they try for another record high for a benchmark futures contract.
Market players now have their sights set on 127.00, a trader for a long-term credit bank said.

JGBs may be capped on the upper side, however, as traders become increasingly cautious of the current high price levels, said a trader for a long-term credit bank's securities affiliate. A rise in U.S. Treasuries overnight should provide momentum to JGBs, traders said.
The 6-3/4 percent 30-year U.S. Treasury bond finished at 102-4/32 on Tuesday, up a full point to yield 6.59 percent versus Monday's closing yield of 6.66 percent.
Results of the U.S. presidential elections are not expected to have any direct effect on the JGB market.
"I don't think the election will change the firm overall trend of the (JGB) market," the second trader said.
The trader said that the market will be watching a speech by the Bank of Japan governor due at 12.40 p.m. (0340 GMT), although this is not expected to be a source of fresh factors.
